quickAnswerHtml: Chai is a Bib Gourmand restaurant in the MICHELIN Guide Thailand 2026, in the Soi Samakkhi 38, Tha Sai, Mueang Nonthaburi area, with a budget of around THB 250–500. No reservations — join the queue outside

blocks.html:
Chai Phochana, or simply "Chai" as MICHELIN calls it, is a late-night khao tom and seafood house hidden away on Soi Samakkhi 38, Tha Sai subdistrict, Mueang Nonthaburi — a location you'd almost never drive past unless someone showed you the way. And yet this restaurant has held a Bib Gourmand in the MICHELIN Guide Thailand every year since 2019, all the way through to the 2026 edition, which says a lot, because a Bib Gourmand is the award for restaurants that deliver "great food at a great price," and holding that position for seven years straight means the kitchen has never let its standards slip. MICHELIN also describes it as spacious and well-organised, which matches the reality of a large khao tom house that opens at 3pm and runs until 1am, taking in customers in waves all night long.

The heart of the place is khao tom kuy-style seafood cooked with more care than the prices suggest. The dish both MICHELIN and diners agree on is the fried grouper with fish sauce — crisp skin, tender flesh — at THB 390, a generous price for a whole fish. Next comes squid stir-fried with salted egg, squid in fish sauce at THB 230, crab fried rice at THB 75, tom yum with fish roe at THB 350, marinated raw crab at THB 360, and the biggest dish on the table, curry-powder sea crab, at THB 800. For anyone showing up late at night, a bowl of hot seafood khao tom is exactly the reason this place exists in the first place. Average spend per head runs only around THB 250–500, enough for several dishes without overthinking it. The atmosphere is an unpretentious seafood house with both a regular zone and an air-con zone, plus its own car park — important, since this location isn't within walking distance of any train station.

What makes Chai Phochana more interesting than your average khao tom shop is that MICHELIN has tagged it "worth queueing for" — the queue is worth the wait — with the busiest stretch early evening, but because the kitchen works fast and the restaurant is large, tables turn over quickly, so the wait is shorter than you'd expect. One more thing to know before you go: the restaurant takes cash only per the MICHELIN listing, and it's closed on the second and fourth Tuesday of every month. If you drive over on a night it's open, land a table, and get that fried grouper with fish sauce set down in front of you — that night alone makes the trip to Nonthaburi worth it.

blocks.name: Chai
blocks.descHtml:
Budget per head around THB 250–500 is light for a Bib Gourmand-level restaurant — crab fried rice starts at THB 75, squid in fish sauce THB 230, fried grouper with fish sauce THB 390, and the large curry-powder sea crab THB 800. The restaurant takes cash only, so bring enough. Most tables are walk-in, but if you're coming as a larger group you can call ahead at 063-998-3986 or 088-978-1558 — no deposit needed, and no online queue system to fight over.

The restaurant is open 15:00–01:00 (Sundays until around midnight) and closed on the second and fourth Tuesday of every month. Early evening is busiest, so if you'd rather skip the wait, go in the late afternoon or after 9pm. Getting there means driving or taking a taxi to Soi Samakkhi 38, Tha Sai, Mueang Nonthaburi, since the MRT Pink Line's Samakkhi station is over 2 km away — too far to walk. On the plus side, the restaurant has its own car park and an air-con zone to sit in.

faq.q: Do I need to book ahead?
faq.a: Mostly walk-in — the restaurant is large and tables turn over quickly. But if you're coming as a bigger group, you can call ahead at 063-998-3986 or 088-978-1558 — just remember the restaurant takes cash only

Around THB 250–500 per person. Crab fried rice is THB 75 a plate, fried grouper with fish sauce is THB 390, and even if you order the THB 800 curry-powder sea crab to share across the table, it's still good value

Fried grouper with fish sauce is the flagship dish, followed by squid stir-fried with salted egg, curry-powder sea crab, and finishing with a bowl of hot seafood khao tom in classic late-night khao tom style

faq.q: How do I get there, and what time should I go?
faq.a: Drive or take a taxi to Soi Samakkhi 38, Tha Sai, Nonthaburi (MRT Samakkhi station is over 2 km away — too far to walk). The restaurant has its own car park and is open 15:00–01:00; early evening is busiest, so late afternoon or after 9pm is more comfortable. Just check it's not the 2nd or 4th Tuesday of the month, when the restaurant is closed
